sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Cenchrus ciliaris is a tufted perennial grass native to warm, dry regions from Africa to South Asia. Its culms are about 10–150 cm tall and leaves 2–13 mm wide. It grows in savannas and open dry places, often on sandy soils.

sections.title: Inflorescence and uses
sections.text: Its dense 2–14 cm false spike bears groups of spikelets surrounded by bristles; the true grain is a small caryopsis. It is widely sown as drought-tolerant forage, but can become invasive where introduced. The plate matches the tuft and bristly cylindrical inflorescences.
